utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon to some familiar faces. We have just signed orders for the attendances of certain young people in the gallery, so, yes. Is there any matter that needs to be raised before we continue with the witness? Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the current scheduling plan for this week has budgeted today through Thursday, if necessary, for -- to complete the evidence of Witness Hutsch. I have a very short time ago I received a e-mail that was forwarded to me from the Victims and Witness Unit, in which Mr. Hutsch informed the members of the Victims and Witness Unit that "I have to leave on Thursday," to go to a third country where Mr. Hutsch has a professional commitment. The e-mail -- the message is not clear whether by leaving on Thursday Mr. Hutsch is referring to after 1345 on Thursday, or at a earlier time. So I have asked the members of the Victims and Witness Unit to try to establish the precise meaning of this message from Mr. Hutsch, so, if necessary, I can bring any problem to the attention of the chamber and the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Given the lengths to which efforts have been made to accommodate Mr. Hutsch, I think it should be fairly clear to him or made clear to him, that he is to give evidence on Thursday, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was, to my knowledge made clear to him several times that he needed to be here Monday through Thursday of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: By the same token, the Chamber would emphasise that it is, if necessary, because we really on our timing, would anticipate that the evidence of Mr. Hutsch should finish Wednesday evening, and Thursday is a fallback in case things are going slower than planned. So I would like counsel to look at the end of Wednesday evening as the time when they should be able to finish with Mr. Hutsch, bearing in mind the time we spent with him earlier. Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. There are two very short applications which we would make at this stage. One of them may sort of spoil the order just made or the recommendation just made by the Chamber. Tomorrow I would have to attend to a appeal matter in the Halilovic case at 2.15 in the afternoon. Considering that tomorrow morning I will be in court all day with a view to cross-examine Mr. Hutsch, I wish to make a application to the Court to see whether the Chamber would be minded not to sit during the last session of the morning or at the least to allow to cut it short perhaps by half an hour with a view to permit me to spend some time with Mr. Halilovic tomorrow morning before the appeals hearing. Mr. Halilovic will be arriving tonight after this session. The second matter, Your Honour, which we would like to apply for at this stage is to make a short application for a brief extension of time. We were supposed today to file our response to the Prosecution motion to amend the indictment. Due to a large amount of work during the past week and preparation in particular of the two present witness, we have encountered some difficulties to be able to file the motion in the course of this day. And we would simply make an application, if possible, for a extension for two days until Wednesday so that the response could be filed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have two further days, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With respect to your first motion, the Chamber would of course try to accommodate you. Given the timing of schedules, if we're able to stretch favours with the people responsible for sound and video recording, we may be able to get one hour 40 minute sessions. If we had two of those we could finish, I believe, at about ten past or quarter past 1.00, after two full one hour 40 minute sessions. And that then would minimise the loss of time and not jeopardise our hope of finishing Mr. Hutsch by the following evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But one way or another, we will finish sometime around 1.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If there is no other matter, if Mr. Hutsch could be brought back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think used the words "Wednesday evening," I meant to say at the end of the Wednesday session, which would bring us to 1.45 Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, welcome back. In view of the lapse of time I think it would be preferable to re-administer the affirmation. If the court officer would be good enough to give you the card for your affirmation. If you would read aloud the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down now. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will recall, Mr. Hutsch, that when we left off sometime ago I was asking you questions about a particle article that had been written in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung about your testimony in the Milosevic case. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an article about a story about Cesa Iri [phoen], not about the article was just a part of this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this article was written by Mr. Rub, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I had been drawing your attention to a number of passages of this articles; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like the registry to show you another part of that article. That is Rule 65 ter 1D280. It is 1D00-2799 for the German original.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that piece, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask the registry to turn to the third page that would be 1D00-2804. I'd like to read a paragraph, Mr. Hutsch. It would be the previous page, please. Thank you. And in the English version it would be 1D00-2804, please. Mr. Hutsch, I will read to you a passage of this article of Mr. Rub where he comments about you. And it says this: "It cannot be surprising that Hutsch became a star in some Serbian media after such testimonies in The Hague. Because of this, he continues with the conspiracy theory which is popular in Serbia and now also more and more popular in Germany. The war about Kosovo was just a rehearsal for the attack on Iraq. The invasion of Iraq is exactly the same as the bombing of Yugoslavia to the smallest details." Do you recall that Mr. Rub suggested that you were propagating conspiracy theories at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rub was wrong because he was quoting a quote from General Lokweit [phoen] that I published I think half a year before and he didn't mark exactly this sentence as a quote from this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you recall that that is the statement he made about you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was doing this statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can look the bottom of the page, please, in the English it starts with the word: "By the way." He also said this: "By the way, it is also Hutsch's idea the Bosnian Muslims as well as the Kosovo Albanian Muslims are connected to the radical Islamic terror groups, the classic story of the Serbian national propaganda, with that, the ethnic cleansings and mass killings of Bosnians and Albanians can be explained as prevention against the Islamic terrorists. With such stories, one can surf on the anti-American wave which is passing through many German and European media. Hutsch and the Horta Journal have picked an especially nice wave." Do you recall Rub making those pretty serious allegations against you as well?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Rub was writing that, but I there was also a translating mistake in this, because Mr. Rub is writing about a insinuation and not about an idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you recall that following that article you had a number of other problems not relating to that article but to your particular story. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell this Chamber what sort of problems you had?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had discussions with some journalists and also discussions with some clients of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also had some legal issues relating to this; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell this Chamber what those were?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to -- to find out -- not to find out. To forbid this article after the German press law.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you were interviewed a second time by the Office of the Prosecutor in July and then December of 2006. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at that time do you recall telling them that your legal or judicial problems were over? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But that was not quite true, was it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is it correct that you had legal matters with Mr. Rub at some stage?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I told to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung as well, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell this Chamber what sort of legal problems you had with them?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had to fight before the land court or land court, I think it is land court and the supreme court in Hamburg about this article and in both courts, Chambers decided that this article was wrong and they were also giving the reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're going to come back to this first issue, sir, but when are you saying that your legal problems with Mr. Rub and the FAZ finished?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the last trial of the Chamber was in July 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall saying this when you were interviewed by the Prosecution in December of 2006: "In paragraph 10 of my first statement, I mentioned court proceedings involving me in German Courts. I wish to add now that I have been discharged and exonerated and the proceedings have been dropped." Can you recall saying that to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in fact in your original statement and paragraph 10 to which you refer, you have made no reference whatsoever to court proceedings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in December of 2006, you told the Office of the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Out of fairness to the witness, wouldn't it be fair to show the witness his statement and show paragraph 10 to which my learned colleague is referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D234.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is your statement, your second statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, and I will ask the registry, please, to turn to the third page of that document. That will be 1 -- well, first we'll start with the second statement. I apologise. This is 1D235. And if we can one to the second page of 1D235, please. And if we can focus on paragraph 5 of that statement, please. Mr. Hutsch, what I'm about to show you is a paragraph taken from your statement of July 2006 and 9 December 2006. And it says this: "In paragraph 10 of my first statement I mentioned court proceedings involving me in German Courts. I wish to add now that I have been discharged and exonerated and the proceedings have been dropped."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry can now bring 1D234, please. And go to page 3, please. This would be 1D00-2569.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is your first statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. It dates from 25th, 6th and 7th of August of 2005. This is the paragraph to which you referred in your second statement and I will let you go through it. And I'll ask you where you mention any court proceedings, and in particular any court proceedings that would relate to your legal situation with the FAZ and the -- Mr. Rub. Do you agree that there is no such reference there?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So in fact during your first statement you had not mentioned any court proceedings that involved you in relation to that story. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, because it was started I think in September 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you said in your second statement is also incorrect as a result. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. First, my interview in front of the investigator was in August 2005. So we started with the legal process in Germany in September 2005. As far as I know, that's correct, what I said, because there was no proceeding going on. And the second is that in December 2006, the -- the legal fight was finished, and we just was working the -- the lawyers were working on compromise. No, not a compromise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A settlement. Agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An Agreement, an agreement like to correct this article in FAZ and they were fighting for the words for this following article. So the legal process already was finished in December 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But that is not quite the case, sir. First you mentioned in your second article that you had mentioned court proceedings and that was not the case. But also this is what the situation is, and I will come back to this negotiation which you have mentioned. The court proceedings were pending until that time when your lawyer and the lawyer of the FAZ reached an agreement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not, that was not correct, because it was -- it was finished with -- with this agreement between the lawyers and the judge said, he finished in this moment the law proceedings and he said that the lawyers had to agree or to -- to create an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that this agreement you're referring to was reached sometime in June 2007, about two weeks or so before you appeared in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's wrong because that was just the moment of the publishing. What I think is this agreement was arranged -- I don't know exactly, but I think it was April. We have to call the lawyer, if it is important for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that in March or April of this year, the Prosecution asked you on behalf of the Defence to provide information about those court proceedings. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall what your answer was to that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that what was going on in this proceeding has nothing to do with this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the answer to my question is that you refused to provide this information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information are open in the Internet for everybody to research, as well for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the Office of the Prosecutor knew about your legal problems and discussion with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they were also aware of your lawsuit against Mr. Rub. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you mentioned already that you had taken steps to obtain a binding order or restraining order to prevent the publication of this article before the courts in Hamburg. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you did afterwards also is to sue the FAZ and Mr. Rub for damage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you perhaps tell this Chamber what sort of reparation or compensation you were seeking from Mr. Rub?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not see the relevance of this particular line of inquiry. Can my learned friend perhaps explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will only do so if directed to do so. I think the objection already been taken the last time and was decided already by the Trial Chamber, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It had been decided in a context that has now changed and you're now pursuing even further this issue and it is getting less apparent why it is relevant, so I think you had better.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honour, I will simply indicate that I believe within the next five minutes we will understand why those are directly related to these proceedings and I have reasons to believe that the Prosecution knows as well what the relationship between those proceedings, and I'm talking of the Boskoski trial, and this lawsuit is, so with the leave of the Chamber I would pursue this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean that you have consciously looked at this issue and believe that the line you are pursuing is relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And if pursued, in a short time it bill become apparent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you should be allowed to continue in that circumstance, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Hutsch, but could you tell this Trial Chamber what remedy or compensation you sought to obtain from Mr. Rub and the FAZ?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning there was the discussion first to correct this article, second, to pay the money that definitely I lost because this article was published.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that there were also other requests that were made by you, Mr. Hutsch, other things which you wanted in this correction article, apart from what you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no other request.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Hutsch, that you insisted that the fact of your appearance as a witness in this case should be expressly mentioned in the piece. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree also that in the course of the --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree also. I agree -- I didn't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you clarify your answer. Do you mean you made that request or you didn't make that specific request?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make this specific request. And that's -- I answered, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if the lawyers of the FAZ or your lawyers were asked to produce the various documents, sir, that they exchanged during those negotiation there would be no such request made on your behalf. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that you asked for the assistance of the Office of the Prosecution in relation to your legal problems?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself, I didn't ask the Office of the Prosecution for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did your lawyer perhaps ask for the assistance of the Office of the Prosecution in this matter?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you obtain assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly ask the Defence counsel and the witness to pause between the questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you tell this Chamber what sort of assistance you received from the Office of the Prosecution in relation to your legal matters?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the -- Ms. Del Ponte wrote a letter where she said that I was a honourful [sic] witness in the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact she reacted against the insinuation of professional dishonesty on your part. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the reason why it was felt that Ms. Del Ponte should get involved in this matter was because of the insinuations or the statements that were made by Mr. Rub and the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung that you were a fabricator and a dishonest person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that in her letter Ms. Del Ponte insisted that she may in fact call you as a witness in any of the Prosecution's case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the letter that Mrs. Del Ponte was writing. I think you have to ask my lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But surely you have seen the article which was published in the FAZ, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw one of the first concepts for this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So are you saying that you didn't see the full version once it was published?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before it was published, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can assist you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D370. It is 1D00-3489 in the English, and the German original is 1D00-3488.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, is that correct before we look at this letter that there is only two things in the article that the FAZ agreed to clarify or specify and that was the fact that they had suggested in the article that the word "murder" only came to your lips when referring to Serbian policemen and the other matter was your suggestion that the people had been not massacred but -- or their body massacred but they had been attacked by dogs. Is that correct? That is the only two things which they agreed to qualify?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is incorrect. That's just the two things they published. But like you said, if you just will take all the documents that the two courts in Hamburg produced to these things you will find a couple of around 20, 25 points just in this article they -- the judges said they were false.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the letter what they published. And I mean, as you can see there is the FAZ and Frans-Josef Hutsch. It says accord or comparison from the German and in the first paragraph it refers to the following: "In May of 2005, Horta Journal wrote about the certain report, Hutsch being co-author of it, under the title "In Doubts With the Accused Milosevic." And it says: The report, among others, says that to Hutsch, as defence witness of the former Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic, who died in between before the war crime tribunal in The Hague in his testimony the word 'murder' only went across his lips as the Serbian policemen were murdered by UCK. Actually, in his testimony, Hutsch did indeed depict the Serbian atrocities in a drastic way also. Then it goes on to say: "The issue of the report was also the Hutsch's testimony on the massacre in Racak whereby this press accused Hutsch that he hardened in the circumstances that the corpse found in Racak were not dismembered by other people but by stray dogs. Within this context one could clearly claim that this corresponds to the report assembled by the forensic team having examined the corpse and which was interrogated by the EU." And then says this: "The main Prosecutor of the criminal tribunal in The Hague, Carla Del Ponte, has in the meantime expressed her opinion to the subject that Mr. Hutsch was a well-balanced and honourable witness who should testify as a Prosecutor witness in cases against the war criminals of the Yugoslavia conflict also in the future. Accordingly, Hutsch so testify before the criminal Tribunal on 17 June 2007 as a Prosecutor witness in case against the former Macedonian minister of the interior, Ljube Boskoski." Is that correct, Mr. Hutsch, that this last sentence was included by you and at your express request. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if someone were to claim that this was the case, you would say that he is incorrect. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect, because probably it was done by my -- my lawyer, but definitely not with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that you saw this trial, as you did with the Milosevic trial, as a opportunity to make publicity for yourself. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you see this trial as a opportunity to make up stories and have them published in newspapers as you did in the Milosevic trial. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage we will simply make a notification for the record. We still haven't received the letter of Madam Del Ponte. We have made requests to the Office of the Prosecutor for Rule 68 disclosure and have given several indications to the Prosecution to the effect that the credibility and reliability of the witness was a big issue in this case. We raise it at this stage and we'll raise it again after the end of this witness in relation to other recent disclosure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to say, first of all, on behalf of the Prosecution, that I was not aware of this letter that was sent by Carla Del Ponte nor have I ever seen this letter. I will now search for the letter and see if I can obtain it and provide it to the -- the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, if time permits I will come back on some of the other stories which you have published at some stage. But at this stage I would like to focus on the events of Ljuboten. And before I do that I am required by the rule to put the Defence case to you. And the Defence case is this: I'm putting it to you, Mr. Hutsch, that you are a fabricator. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you, Mr. Hutsch, that have you given false evidence to this Tribunal. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm putting it to you that events and incidents which you have described as events or incidents that you had personally witnessed or seen were in fact stories that you pieced back together from information that you collected from other people. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, we'll go, if you permit, in reverse order and we'll start with evidence which you've given about the 14th of August. That would be the Tuesday, if you can recall, 14th of August of 2001. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I think, Your Honour, we came to a point where it is absolutely necessary that I will continue my testimony in my mother language. Because the defender is manipulating in various ways my testimony. He is taking -- he is breaking up parts of this testimony and is presenting that to the Chamber but he isn't lightening the whole context and I think it is absolutely necessary to continue in my mother language, because, yeah, it is necessary to answer in a most precise way to the questions of the defender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The effect of that will necessitate, I fear, some delay. The request is not unreasonable, and we have appreciated Mr. Hutsch's efforts to deal with the matter in English, which is not his first language. Your cross-examination, not reflecting upon it, has often been one which requires very precise understanding of language, and that being so, Mr. Hutsch feels he is at a disadvantage. I would ask, if you would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are in the process of finding out how long it will be before German interpretation can be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps to use the free time, we would simply indicate if the Chamber were minded to have a double session on Wednesday morning and afternoon and if it were possible, we would be willing to -- or capable of doing that, if that became a problem. Simply an indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Mettraux that you have found a free courtroom tomorrow afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that was wishful thinking. What we were saying is that if there is a courtroom, we would be definitely willing and capable of doing it. The alternative, Your Honour, if Your Honour were minded to do that, is I believe that after the Halilovic appeal, there may be some space available and that would also be agreeable to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Another trial is listed following the Halilovic appeal. So that that is not possible. We cannot obtain any German interpretation this afternoon. The possibility of obtaining it for tomorrow is being explored. German is not a language that we do not regularly use. So that if we were to adjourn now because of the interpretation, we will lose the balance of today and perhaps tomorrow. So that's the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just as a alternative to loosing time, would the Chamber prefer that the Prosecution call back Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm trying at the moment, the Chamber is concerned that we not only continue with Mr. Hutsch but in fairness to him and everybody, that we try to finish his evidence in the time available. I wish to explore with you Mr. Mettraux a further possibility. You have been pursuing with very precise questioning an issue concerning the content of a newspaper article and legal proceedings concerning it and a correction or a further publication concerning that. In other areas of the factual evidence, I think Mr. Hutsch would not be at a language disability continuing in English. It is this area where language which is very precise is important to Mr. Hutsch. Is it possible for us to continue in other areas of cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I was over in any case with the issue pertaining to the newspaper. It may come back at a later stage but it can certainly be postponed until that time when we have German translation available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hutsch, as you can -- you have been able to follow, I think, what has been happening. The Chamber fully accepts that if you were to be subject to more precise cross-examination concerning the article in the German newspaper and the legal proceedings, that, in fairness to you, you should have the opportunity to speak in your mother language. It is possible, though -- it is not possible to do that now. It may be possible to do it by tomorrow or certainly by the day following. If Mr. Mettraux leaves that area alone and continues with some other areas, would you be prepared to carry on in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we can try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Because one of the hopes is that we can finish the evidence in time to let you get away when you want to get away, and if we can continue using English over some other topics, that will assist that happening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just to make clear, Your Honour, every topic the defender was mentioning till now and he touched till now, he was breaking up just parts like a puzzle but he is presenting just the puzzles and the pieces to you and not the complete material and that's what I think is shameful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, shall we say that that is part of the process of questioning. We are conscious that that process should be done fairly. And if it is apparent that there would be a language difficulty in hampering your answers, we would certainly not be content to allow that to occur. We can see that possibility with the question of the article in the German newspaper and the legal proceedings. There are other areas where questioning will occur, you may want to say more than the question allows. That can be dealt with in two ways. Either you say that the question doesn't present the complete picture and say more or just say, well, the answer to your question is this, but much more needs to be said about that and it will then be a matter which Mr. Saxon could return to in re-examination, if he thought it adequate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay. With Mr. Hutsch's cooperation, and subject to the possibility that he may find some other areas presenting language difficulty, we are able to continue. Thank you Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, as I indicated I would like to ask you a number of questions about the 14th of August of 2001, and just to refresh your memory that would be the Tuesday that followed the events in Ljuboten. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have indicated both when you talked to the Prosecution and in your evidence in chief that on that day, you said you had visited the village of Ljuboten. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall indicating as well that on that day, the 14th, you had spent the rest of the day in or around Skopje, before and after. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have indicated, I believe, that this visit on the 14th was the second of two visits which you said you made to the village, the first visit having been on the 12th. That would be the Sunday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said that during the second visit, the 14th, the Tuesday, you were accompanied by two interpreters, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask you to name those two persons, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, you know this Jonathan Wendell decision of the [indiscernible] Tribunal. We don't have to discuss that anymore, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, I will ask you once again. Can you please give the name of the two people who you claim accompanied you on your visit during the 14th?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, I have to cover my informations and my sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch has been asked this question several times now both by the Prosecution and by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're aware of that, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Mettraux has asked. It is becoming repetitive, but in view of the break he is certainly properly within his realm to ask again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think I will move on this one. We will come back to the issue of his -- Mr. Hutsch's sources, as he calls them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But at this stage, Mr. Hutsch, is that correct that on the 14th of August of 2001, you said that you went to the village with other journalists? Do you recall saying that to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said there were other journalists there. I didn't tell them that I was going with this journalist to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall telling the Office of the Prosecutor as well that there were representatives of Human Rights Watch in the village on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, I believe, to the Office of the Prosecutor and to this Court that on that day, you had kept a notebook or reporter's notes as you had done, you say, on the 12th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was the document that you showed -- that was shown to you by the Prosecution in your examination in chief, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in this document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and the witness please observe a pause between answer and question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, we have just been asked to try to pause between questions an answers. And, Mr. Hutsch, is that correct that in these reporter's notes of the 14th of August you recorded what you said was your interview with Mr. Elmaz Jusufi, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you indicated that this interview which you say you had with Mr. Jusufi took place in the village of Ljuboten in his home. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also indicated to this Trial Chamber and to the Office of the Prosecutor that on the 14th of August of 2001, you also claimed to have interviewed a person called Aziz Bajrami. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll turn to your notes in a minute, Mr. Hutsch, so that can you look for yourself. But is that correct that you are suggesting that both of those interviews took place in Ljuboten on that date, the 14th? That's what you told this Chamber. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think Mr. Hutsch says he would like to be shown --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I can do, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- to be reminded.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- Hutsch, is I can read the relevant passage in your examination in chief. This will be the 28th of June of 2007. It be page 2806, 2807. And this is an exchange between yourself and the Prosecutor, Mr. Saxon, and you were being shown these notes of the 14th of August of 2001. I believe they are exhibit P320. And I will show them to you in a minute. And Mr. Saxon asked you this: "And this is information -- is this information that you received from Aziz Bajrami on the 14th?" "Yes, that is." That is page 2806. And then at the bottom of the page it says this, Mr. Saxon again: "Is this the information that Aziz Bajrami gave you on the 14th of August?" "Yes, that is." And if I can be of further assistance to you, I will ask the registry to bring up what is exhibit P320. Do you recognise this document, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the first page you will see there's a reference to Mr. Jusufi, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page? In the English, please, at this stage. The second page in English would be N003-0016-ET-02. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see, Mr. Hutsch, the other reference to Mr. Aziz Bajrami --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- that you made in response to Mr. Saxon. Does that help you to refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you say with whom you say you went on the -- on these two interviews which you have mentioned to Mr. Saxon, the interview with Mr. Elmaz Jusufi and the interview with Mr. Aziz Bajrami? Did anyone accompany you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, you were asking me if I was doing these two interviews in Ljuboten. And you presented me now two paragraphs from my older testimony. And I don't find in this testimony that I said that I was doing these interviews in Ljuboten. I'm not finding that, sorry. But you were asking me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, isn't that what you told the Prosecution in your evidence in chief, Mr. Hutsch? Are you suggesting that those two interviews took place anywhere else when you just told me you had interviewed Mr. Elmaz Jusufi in front of his house? Are you now trying to tell us something else?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, I think we were interviewing in front of his house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about Mr. Bajrami, are you suggesting that it took place somewhere else, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does it mean "suggesting" in this context?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me ask you this way: Did you or did you not interview Mr. Aziz Bajrami on the 14th of August of 2001, in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't interview Mr. Bajrami in the interview in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So can you tell this Chamber where you say now you interviewed Mr. Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it because you can't remember, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it was in the house of -- of one source that needs to be protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And where does that source live, Mr. Hutsch, is that in Ljuboten or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your evidence at this stage, Mr. Hutsch, is that you interviewed Mr. Elmaz Jusufi on the 14th in the village of Ljuboten and that you interviewed Mr. Aziz Bajrami in another place which you are declining to identify and you're also declining to identify the source which you say lent his or her place to interview him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come back to that, but first I'm going to put this to you, sir. Isn't that correct that you had never either interview with either Mr. Elmaz Jusufi, as you claim, or Mr. Aziz Bajrami, as you also claim, but that you made those up based on information that you obtained from other sources. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm putting to you that one of the main sources for the content of this document is a report prepared by the organisation Human Rights Watch. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber at what time you arrived on the 14th of August of 2001, you say, in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, in the morning, I had breakfast together with two colleagues, then I had a phone call because the Ohrid Agreement was signed, I think, on the 13th. Some phone calls. I think we entered the village between 1.00 and 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stood there for 45 minutes. I think 45 minutes, yes. Maximum 60 minutes because the newspaper wasn't interested in this story.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Hutsch. Are you suggesting that within that hour you contacted your newspaper and asked them whether they would be interested or not. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: My evidence is that I got a phone call from my section, from the head of the political section who told me that I had to investigate much more about the Ohrid Agreement and the role German troops may play in the realisation of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So sometimes between 2.00 or 3.00 in the afternoon you left Ljuboten again, you say. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during that time you say you stayed with your two interpreters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you went back to Skopje, correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you go back to your hotel or what did you do when you went back to Skopje?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried -- I started to investigate the story about the Ohrid Agreement. I think I published as well in this day a story about the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you spend the evening in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was spending the evening in Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the next day, on the 15th, Mr. Hutsch, do you remember where you were?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you had travelled to other places? Were you still in Macedonia at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the rest of the week? Can you recall, were you still in Macedonia at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I left Macedonia on Friday, if my -- if my memories are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that would be the 18th. Or 17th. 17th.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal answer].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me put this to you, then, Mr. Hutsch. In paragraph 151 of your statement you had told the Prosecution that you had met Mr. Jusufi at his home in Ljuboten. Do you recall telling them that and reiterating this here in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you show me?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be Rule 65 ter 1D234. This would be page 1D00-2587. And as you will see, Mr. Hutsch, you have given the same indication as you gave earlier in this courtroom where you say: "I also visited the crime scene where Rami Jusufi was killed. I spoke with his father, Elmaz Jusufi." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can we now turn to what is tab 31 of the binder, and that would be again your notes, your reporter's notes of the 14th of August of 2001. That's Exhibit P320. Thank you. Do you recognise this document again, Mr. Hutsch? This is the same as I showed you a bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if one may go one page forward in the German but not the English, please. You'll recall, Mr. Hutsch, about being asked about a little drawing on the second page of the German which is on the first page of the English in summary fashion, this drawing. Do you remember me -- do you remember Mr. Saxon asking you questions about that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask you to focus on the record in the English of this document or in the German. It can be moved one page forward for Mr. Hutsch, if he prefers to read in the German. And it records the following, Mr. Hutsch, as you can see. The first thing it records at the top lefthand is it records the fact, Ljuboten. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may go to the next page, please, in both languages. And that's the place where you had the interview, is that correct? Is that correct, Mr. Hutsch? Perhaps we can go to the previous page so Mr. Hutsch can have a look at it again. Do you see, Mr. Hutsch, that there's a time and a place in your note and it says: "Ljuboten 9.45." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So this is the place and the time that you noted regarding your interview with Mr. Jusufi, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So what does this time and place refer to then, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the point that I said we have to go to Ljuboten and I was asking the interpreters from 9.45 to have a meeting in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are saying that this note on the top of the page doesn't reflect the start of your interview but the meetings which you had that day with your interpreter. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we please turn to the next page. Do you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that there's no other time and no other place mentioned prior to the interview which you say you had with Mr. Bajrami? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can go back to the first page, and I apologise to the registry for moving back and forth. I'd like to read the annotations which you made of what you say was your interview with Mr. Elmaz Jusufi. If the registry could focus a bit on the bottom of the page, please. Thank you. It says this: "Elmaz Jusufi, 58, son Rami, 33, shot by MUP, Ministry of Interior, members on Sunday, car destroyed. MUP uniformed but not masked enter the property around 8.20 hour through the front yard. Around 20 of them were in the front yard. Rami reportedly tried to lock front door, which was open. The police in the front yard reportedly threw hand-grenades. Machine-gun was reportedly set up against gate." And if we can turn to the next page, please. The next annotation says this, Mr. Hutsch: "As son turned around to go back into the living-room a strong explosion reportedly occurred. The door was reportedly blasted open. Rami was riddled, hail of bullets, Rami was hit in side and stomach. MUP then reportedly poured petrol on the car, Zastava, and set fire to it." Then there's a little drawing. And then says: "MUP reportedly entered the house around 10.30, about three policemen who then proceeded to fire in the direction of Ljuboten. Witness Elmaz Jusufi, friend," and then a beginning of a telephone number, "MUP members then reportedly shouted 'we are going to kill you all.'" Mr. Hutsch, is it your evidence before this Chamber that this reflects the interview which you say you had with Mr. Elmaz Jusufi on the 14th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what Mr. Jusufi told my interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting it to you that you never had an interview with Mr. Elmaz Jusufi on the 14th of August of 2001 in Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Hutsch, Mr. Elmaz Jusufi and his wife have testified before this Tribunal, and their evidence makes it impossible for you to have had this interview with them. And I would like to read to you first what Ms. Jusufi, the wife of Elmaz, said to this Tribunal about this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is at -- on the transcript on the 7th of May of 2007. It is at page 450. And she is describing what happened in the house at the time and she is talking about the day when Rami Jusufi was killed. And she said this: "We took his body to my daughter's house in the early morning hour, 1.00 or 2.00. But when he died, he was in my own house. I don't know why this has been recorded in this way." And then there's a question to Ms. Jusufi, and it says: "And if I were again to tell you, Ms. Jusufi, that you went to the house of your daughter on Saturday evening together with your daughter-in-law and your grandchildren," and she answered this: "No, no, I didn't go there on Saturday. That's not correct. I didn't go to my daughter's house on Saturday. I was in my house. What you're saying is a mistake. You're putting things the way you like them." And then there was a further question: "At the end, Ms. Jusufi, in your house in the village of Ljuboten, to that house, you have returned only a month later when your son was buried again in the graveyard in Ljuboten, is that correct?" "Yes. Well, we were afraid to take him to the graveyard. There was no place we could take him." So what Ms. Jusufi told this Chamber is that she and the body of Rami, in any case, left in the early hours of what she said was the 134th of August of 2001, that's the Monday, that she went to the house of her daughter and that she didn't return to her house for an entire month. Do you agree with that, that's in substance what she says.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then I'd like to show you another part of the evidence which was given before this Tribunal and this time this is the evidence of Mr. Rami Jusufi, I'm sorry, Elmaz Jusufi himself, and it is the transcript of the 8th of May of 2007. The page is 510. This is the exchange. The question is: "Do you recall, Mr. Jusufi, that after this interview which you went with Muzafer Jusufi, the representatives of Human Rights Watch made that on the 23rd of August they visited your house, made some photographs and you had still not returned. You were still not returned to your house then." And then he answers: Muzafer was in Skopje. We'd stayed in Skopje for more than a month, for about 45 days. I don't know who gave the other statements. I have given my own statement. Muzafer did not come back to Ljuboten for five months. He stayed in Skopje." Then he is asked: "But you are certain that you did not return for the following three or four week to your house, is that correct?" "Six weeks, six full weeks. Now, whether six weeks makes 50 years or 45, that, I don't know. But it is six weeks." And: "Neither you" -- I'm sorry. "Neither your wife Zenep had returned to the house?" "No, nobody. " Do you agree, sir, that in line with what his wife had said, Mr. Jusufi had indicated that after what happened to his son, he left his house and did not come back for what he says could be a month, 45 or 55 -- or 50 days, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree, and I'll tell you why, because you are manipulating the Chamber as well, because that what the people said is exactly that what happened. If they say they return to their house, they say they are living in their house again and not that they just was going there for some hours, for example. And as far as you know, on these four teams, they were organised by the citizens of Ljuboten. I don't say a press conference in Ljuboten, but there was -- they were interested to tell their story to journalists, to NGOs and to everybody. So they organised, I will -- the right word in Germany, it was just a press talk, press discussion, something like that. And not a press conference. And as a -- as a citizen of Switzerland like you are, it is right that they didn't return to their house, but they were not living there, and that is what they are saying here. And you are misleading here the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that you are misleading the Chamber and I will put to you the evidence of Mr. Kamberi now, which may assist you in that regard. This is the evidence of the 5th of September of 2007 and it is at page 4591 to 4592. And this is what -- this is an exchange between counsel and Mr. Fatmir Kamberi, who is a villager of Ljuboten. Starts in the middle of the page: "When you returned in the village with some of your friends, you went to the house of Rami Jusufi and helped his father to take the body of Rami Jusufi at his sister's place in the Durmisi neighbourhood, right?" And the answer of Mr. Kamberi is: "That's correct." "And the following morning you yourself attended the funeral of Rami Jusufi in the courtyard of his sister and his ceremony was conducted by the elderly Muslim priest from the village, right?" And it's answer is: "Correct." Then there is a question by counsel. It says this: "However, I'm asking you whether you're familiar with the fact that Elmaz went to Skopje on that day together with his wife and that he remained there for over a month. It looks like the information I had as to where they went in Skopje was not correct." And the answer of Mr. Kamberi: "I don't know myself where they went. They went to Skopje and remained there but where I don't know." And then he is asked further this: "And if you recall in your statement, you stated that you went to the yard of Rami Jusufi's house and that at the moment certain persons from the OSCE were taking photographs of the bullet casings in the yard. Do you remember this?" And he said: "Yes, I do. And that, Mr. Hutsch, refers to the 14th of August in Ljuboten. And then he is being asked: "There was nobody in the house, right, because the father and the mother of Rami Jusufi were already in Skopje, right?" And the answer is: "Correct." So, Mr. Hutsch, it is not just a matter of Mr. Jusufi being in another house in the village where you say you could have found him. He was simply not in Ljuboten on that day. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't find a discrepance [sic] between that what I said and that what you gave me now as a quote. Because like you said and like Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Kamberi.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Kamberi said, there were interviews taken by members of the OSCE, by other journalists. All these journalists can give -- give evidence that I have been there as well, and so where is the problem now, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that what the evidence of Mr. Kamberi reflects is that by the 14th of August when the OSCE was visiting the village, Mr. Jusufi had not returned to the village of Ljuboten and as he and his wife pointed out in their evidence, they did not return to the village for between a month and 50 days? Isn't that what all three people said and agreed upon?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, if I am asking people, for example, even ethnical Macedonians, who had disappeared from their houses, and there were, for example, in front of the parliament, accused will know that, everybody of them told us that they didn't return to their home town because they were not living there but they were going there just to visit to see what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same in Lesok, in the monastery of Leshoq. The people will tell you they didn't return to Lesok but there was there even when there was the big ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, you see, Mr. Hutsch, both Ms. Jusufi and Mr. Jusufi have said that they did not return for a month or 50 days. There may be cases, as you said, where people would say that, but those people have testified before there Tribunal and have said that they had not returned, and what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is you never had that meeting, did you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, I told you that I had this meeting. That's the first. Second is I tried to help you what the meaning of returning is, and, yeah, I think it is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's see where you got your information from, Mr. Hutsch. And I would ask the registry to bring up exhibit P320 once more, please. Sorry, Mr. Hutsch, it has disappeared from my screen. But do you have this in front of yours, on your screen?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just a note, one of the reporter's notes now in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perfect. Well, we will look again at what you say you recorded from your interview, and if the registry could enlarge once again the information which you have recorded in this document. So I will read it out to you once more. It says this: "Ljuboten 9.45. Elmaz Jusufi, 58, son, Rami, 33, shot by MUP, Ministry of Interior members, on Sunday. Car destroyed. MUP uniformed but not masked, enter the property around 0820 hours through the front yard. Around 20 of them were in the front yard. Rami reportedly tried to lock front door, which was open. The police in the front yard reportedly threw hand-grenades, machine-gun was reportedly set up against gate. As son turned around to go back into the living-room, a strong explosion reportedly occurred. Door was reportedly blasted open. Rami was riddled hail of bullets. Rami was hit in side and stomach. MUP then reportedly poured petrol on the car, Zastava, and set fire to it. MUP reportedly entered the house around 1030 hours, about three policemen, who then proceeded to fire in the direction of Ljuboten." Witness, Elmaz Jusufi - friend and a telephone number. "MUP members then reportedly shouted, 'We're going to kill you all.'" Do you recall that I had read that to you already. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that but for a few additions or exaggeration of this information, you had taken it all almost verbatim from the report of Human Rights Watch, is that correct that's where you got that information?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get this information from the Human Rights Watch report because till today, I didn't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we should compare it then to the report and that's exhibit P352, Mr. Hutsch, and I'm putting it to you that you knew exactly what the content of that report is. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 7, please, or, Your Honour, perhaps it would be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be more practical to have the break now and then you can come back to that passage. So we will have the first break now and resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, before we proceed I have been asked to ask you, could you give the name of the lawyer who you say assisted you in those proceedings with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tania Irion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree, Mr. Hutsch, to the confidentiality or any professional confidentiality would that relate to those proceedings to be lifted should either parties wish to obtain that material for the purpose of the present proceedings? Would you accept that the parties, either Mr. Saxon or myself, would have access to the documents that were exchanged between your lawyer and the FAZ and Mr. Rub. Would you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something I would like to decide with my lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I will simply ask you for the record can you confirm whether or not whether the spelling of the lawyers that you've mentioned, which would assist?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. You will recall, Mr. Hutsch, that before the break I had read out to you the notes that you made of what you said was your interview with Mr. Elmaz Jusufi. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what I told you as well, what I'm putting it to you now is that in fact all of that information aside from little additions here and there, you took from the Human Rights Watch report. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown what is exhibit P352. I'll ask the registry to go to page 7 of that document. That would be page U000-0106, please. And that's a report, Mr. Hutsch, that is freely available on the Internet. And I will read the passage to you which starts with the words: "Elmaz Jusufi's home." Can you see that on your screen?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read it out to you. It says this: "Elmaz Jusufi's home was among the first to be attacked. Elmaz Jusufi, a 58-year-old bedridden paraplegic, told Human Rights Watch how the Macedonian police forces blew away the gate of his home, shot dead his 33-year-old son, Rami Jusufi, through the front door of the home and then torched his car." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And before I proceed, Mr. Hutsch, I will ask you to close the notebook on your right which you are using. I understand you would be permitted to take note if you so wished, but I'm grateful. The report goes on to say this, and that's attributed to

utterances.speaker: MR. JUSUFI
utterances.text: "The moment the attack on the village started, they came to my house. My front yard was full with them. There were about 20. They were all in uniform, but not masked. They bombed the gate to the yard. Then my son went to close the front door. At the moment he closed the door and went back into the room, there was a huge explosion. They blew away the door with machine-gun fire. "That was the moment my son was hit in the side and stomach from their shots. He fell down there. It happened right in front of my eyes. The police did not come into the house. I got into my wheelchair and went to close the door and my son. My son was suffering for about two hours. He was in a lot of pain. My car was parked in the front yard, right next to the gate. They poured gasoline on it, and set it on fire. I heard the police say, 'Pour the gasoline.'" And then there's another statement or another summary of a statement that is given to Human Rights Watch by a person called Muzafer Jusufi. Would you agree, sir, that but for the odd details to which I'm going to turn in a minute this information in the Human Rights Watch report is strikingly similar or in fact perfectly similar to what you put in your notes. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. He is -- he is different to mine. The common content is the same, is quite similar, but there are a lot of differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to turn to those differences that I could identify then. Perhaps you can identify others. But would you agree that as far as the age of the people, for instance, that we're given here are the same as in your document, which doesn't mean much, but you agree that it's the case?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that -- but, on the other hand, probably you may explain to me how it can be that Jusufi, Elmaz Jusufi would give a different testimony to two people.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's quite correct. Would it also be correct that the mention of 20 policemen, about 20 policemen is again the same as in your statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And also the details about the uniforms but not masks. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The way in which the door was said to have been blown away and Mr. Jusufi killed?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I noticed that he said there was throwing hand grenades, and from my military experience, a hand-grenade can't blow away a door.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But there you would agree that there is no reference either for or against a hand-grenade. All he says is the door -- there was a huge explosion and they blew away the door with machine-gun fire. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And also what is similar here is the reference to the place in which you say Rami Jusufi had been shot. That is in the side and the stomach. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you've indicated, Mr. Hutsch, there's a number of things which differ between this statement and yours. And you will recall that in your notes you mentioned that at 10.30 three policemen came back at the house and they then proceeded to shoot from the house. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that it is not a claim that is apparent from the statement given by Mr. Jusufi. Do you agree with that? In fact, if I can assist you there, if you go further down the page there is a statement about those three police officers. It starts with the word: "After shooting Rami Jusufi." Can you see that? It is after the quote.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go to the end of that particular line, you will see that this particular comment which is made by Human Rights Watch is in fact not attributed to anyone in that report. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But it is something that has made it into your notes, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's another matter which I would draw to your attention. And it is -- if we can go back to what is exhibit P320. That's, again, your reporter's note, Mr. Hutsch.
