And we could please go to the second page. The second page of the English as well, please. Thank you. And if the top of the page could be enlarged somewhat. I draw your attention, Mr. Hutsch, on the last comment which you say you received from Mr. Jusufi during that interview. It says this: "MUP members then reportedly shouted, 'we are going to kill you all.'" Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But that's not, again, something that you heard from Mr. Jusufi, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the interpreter translated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you where you took it from.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's -- can we go back to P352, please. That's again the Human Rights Watch report and, please, page 7 once again. It is U 000-01-06. I'm grateful. If you could go to the middle of the page which starts with -- yes, thank you. See, Mr. Hutsch, after the comment or statement which was attributed to Mr. Elmaz Jusufi by Human Rights Watch, there's also a statement which is attributed to another person called Muzafer Jusufi, and if you look at the last paragraph in the last line in that paragraph, that is attributed to Mr. Muzafer Jusufi, there is it a sentence starting with the words: "They were swearing at us." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what Mr. Muzafer Jusufi told Human Rights Watch is: "They were swearing at us all the time." Then there is an expletive and it says: "We will kill you all." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see "Motherfuckers, we kill you all."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that. Can you see that at the end of this sentence there is a footnote?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you confirm that this statement about the "we will kill you all" statement is attributed not to Mr. Elmaz Jusufi but to Mr. Muzafer Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree with that? And in fact, Mr. Jusufi never suggested either in his report in his interview with Human Rights Watch or before this Tribunal that he had heard any such things and what you did is you mistakenly picked it up from the statement of another person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What Mr. Elmaz Jusufi recalled from that incident, Mr. Hutsch, is that there were not three policemen that came back but two of them, and none much them entered the house to shoot from it, as you had wrongly, again, suggested, but that they had come to the house and he heard one sentence from them, and that wasn't "We will kill you all." What he heard and the only thing he heard, in his own word is, "Here are only two people," and then he said the policeman turned back and left. That's the transcript on the 8th of May, 2007, page 529. So what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that you have fabricated this story based on the report of Human Rights Watch. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And not only did you fabricate this part of the story with Mr. Elmaz Jusufi, but you did exactly the same with the information which you say from Mr. Aziz Bajrami. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask to you go --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: But probably you may show -- you may explain me how now this sketch that you withhold in this whole argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I can guarantee you, Mr. Hutsch, that nothing will be withheld from you and we will come to the sketch in a minute. I have a lot of question for you about this one. But for the time being, I will ask to you turn to exhibit P320, and that's again your reporter's notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry, please, to turn to the second page of that document. Thank you. And if we can enlarge the part which starts with the words: "Near mosque, Aziz Bajrami."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll read out to you, Mr. Hutsch, the information which you say you've recorded about this interview which you said you had with Mr. Bajrami on the 16th. It says this: "Aziz Bajrami, 66, father of Bekir, Sulejman, 21, Mevludin." And then: "Hid together with eight women of the family in the house of Zija. MUP members reportedly blasted open the door of Zija and stormed the house. They reportedly fired through the door with a machine-gun? (AK 47)." Then there's a comment, I believe, "Zero injured below. Ordered to leave the house. Men with hands to the back of their heads, kneel. Men separated from women. Hand over passports." And then there's a quote: "Don't look up or you're dead. Aziz had his money with him, 3.000 Deutschemark, 7.000 dinars stolen by policemen: "Don't tell anyone. Jewelry belonging to women was also stolen. Jewelry in the family for generations, possessions. Aziz and sons were reportedly ordered to the house of Nexit Ademi. Why? Outside they met young men from the neighbourhood. They all reportedly had T-shirt pulled over their heads. The group was herded together, all kneeled. Sulejman kicked in the head several times. Reportedly began to bleed from the nose. Aziz was reportedly ordered to get up and go home." And if we could turn to the next page, please. Is goes on to say: "Together with Muharem Bajrami, 65, after that, Muharem was reportedly shot," illegible, "soldier border police. MUP members reportedly shouted, 'The pig is still moving,' fresh shots. And then there's: 'Long live Arkan.' Get up A," and then there's a quote: "Go into that house, old man, go back home. All lay down again. Sulejman was kicked again several times. He got up [indiscernible] and tried to run away. Then the Chetnik who had kicked him shot him. Then all started shooting. Aziz was shot in the hand. Do not shoot. He is a soldier ? Macedonian." Do you recall making those notes in your reporter's notes, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that all you did was in fact to lift that information, again, from the Human Rights Watch report for the odd few little changes which you inserted in it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can Mr. Hutsch please be shown exhibit P352.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is again, Mr. Hutsch, the Human Rights Watch report and that would be at page 9, please. It is it U000-0108, please. And I'll ask you, Mr. Hutsch, to locate on this document the third paragraph which starts with the words: "66-year-old Aziz Bajrami." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read it out for you: "66-year-old Aziz Bajrami, the father of two of the men killed and three of the men arrested in Ljuboten that day, was hiding in the basement of his neighbour's Zija's home with his son Bekir, Sulejman, and Mevludin and eight female relatives during the attacks on Sunday. This home was adjacent to the house of Nexit Ademi where between 7 and 9 men and also -- had also been sheltering in the basement." Before I proceed, Mr. Hutsch, you made a comment earlier about the age and your comment was quite right that it would be quite logical that if two people interview the same person they would be given the same age. Isn't that is correct, however, Mr. Hutsch, that the only persons whose age you mentioned in your notes are those which are mentioned in this report. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the only one who was interesting for me in the beginning of a investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But isn't that correct that the only person whose name you mention, for example, 66-year-old Aziz Bajrami, or further down in the text the 21-year-old Sulejman, you mention their age. But none of the others who are not mentioned in the Human Rights Watch report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I see, of the age of Sulejman isn't also not mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you go down the page, Mr. Hutsch, you will see there's a sentence which starts with the word: "Aziz Bajrami." Do you see that? It says: "Aziz Bajrami and his sons were then ordered to lay down next to the men."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Moment. Aziz Bajrami and his three sons were --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No. Further down, two paragraph further down. It is after the quote. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you agree that the 21-year-old age that you mentioned in your notes is also mentioned in this. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go further down in that paragraph you will also see that there's another person whose age you mention, and that's Muharem Bajrami, 68-year-old. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then I'll going on to read the statement of the Human Rights Watch. It says this: "Suddenly, the police burst into Zija's home and started firing into the basement without warning. They started shooting through the door. It wasn't even closed. Loads of shots were fired through the door from machine-guns. No one in the basement was injured. And the police then ordered everyone to come out. When we got out, they separated us men and lined us up, the four of us, kneeling down. They asked for IDs and told us not to look up, not to look to the side, just keep our heads down. The police officer who asked for the IDs noticed that Aziz Bajrami had a significant amount of money in his pocket and stole it. The police officer saw that I had 3.000 German marks and 7.000 Macedonian dinars and took all of the money, telling me, 'Don't tell anybody.' The police also stole gold jewelry, a traditional means of safeguarding savings from the women of the family." Can you follow?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then there's a quote which is attributed to Mr. Bajrami and he says: "Aziz Bajrami and his three sons were then told to walk over to the neighbour's house of Nexit Ademi. They said to stand up and keep our hands behind our heads. Again, they told us not to look up and keep our heads down. They took us to a small a gate between the yards. There were these young men from there from the neighbourhood, neighbouring house, about eight or nine of them. I was trying to look and I saw that they all had their T-shirts over their heads." Can you follow that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on. But would you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that's where you got your information from which matches almost to the word what you have put in your reporter's notes. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's in fact where you got the information from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is as with Elmaz Jusufi, you never interviewed Aziz Bajrami. I'm putting it to you that this is one of your fabrications and I'm also putting it to you that the reason why you thought you were safe to say that because of your belief that Human Rights Watch was in the village on that day, the 14th of August of 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were members of the Human Rights Watch there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that's what you have indicated earlier in your evidence, sir, and that's also what you have told the Office of the Prosecutor upon a request by the Defence to obtain some information. The problem with that, sir, is that Human Rights Watch was not in the village of Ljuboten on the 14th of August of 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm putting it to you that this is yet another fabrication that you have put in your evidence to this Trial Chamber. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you see, Mr. Hutsch, the representative of Human Rights Watch, Mr. Peter Bouckaert, who prepared and wrote this report appeared as a witness in this Tribunal, and he was asked a number of questions about these matters, and he indicated to the Court that before his arrival there had been no representatives of the Human Rights Watch in the village of Ljuboten. Would you agree that this contradicts your evidence, knowing that Mr. Bouckaert arrived on the 17th of August of 2001 in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking whether you knew or not, Mr. Hutsch. What I'm asking you is whether you agree that the evidence of Mr. Bouckaert, if believed on this point, would strongly contradict yours. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- that might be, but it might be a Macedonian representative there, because I don't know exactly where -- who of the journalists gave this information. But one of them said there's also a member of Human Rights Watch there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that you're making false statement on the go. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to read to what you the exchange was between myself and Mr. Bouckaert on that point. This is the 3rd of July of 2007. It is Mr. Peter Bouckaert and the page is 3.022 to 3.023, and the question was this: "Is that correct also that at the time of your arrival, there was no other investigator or researcher of Human Rights Watch on the grounds in Macedonia?" "Yes." "Is that also correct that after the incident in Ljuboten, you were the first representative of Human Rights Watch to visit Ljuboten?" "Yes." You see, Mr. Hutsch, if you had looked more carefully at the report of Human Rights Watch you would have seen in foonote 19 of that document that the visit by Human Rights Watch representatives in the village of Ljuboten took place only on the 23rd of August of 2001. So I'm putting it to you to you once again, Mr. Hutsch, do you agree that this entire story of you going to the village of Ljuboten on the 14th of August of 2001, this entire story of interviewing both Mr. Elmaz Jusufi and Aziz Bajrami is completely false? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you had looked a bit more carefully again at the reports of Human Rights Watch, you would have seen, contrary to your belief that Human Rights Watch had been in the village on the 14th, that Mr. Jusufi was in fact interviewed not on the 14th but on the 20th and not in Ljuboten but in Skopje, because that's where he was. And what you have said is false. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another thing which I would like to ask you after that happened that make your evidence even more improbable. Do you recall that at the beginning your evidence, I asked you a number of questions, general questions about your practice as a journalist. Do you recall those general questions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this was on the 28th of June of 2007, Mr. Hutsch. And one of the question or one of the proposition I put to you was that your practice when you published articles for the Hamburger Adenblatt was to mention the place from which you were writing or you said sometimes researching the article. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is page 2837 of the transcript. And another thing to which you agree is that you would not write an article about a particular place or a particular incident unless you had gone there yourself and, if you hadn't and received information about this place, you said that you would make that clear in the article. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be transcript 2837, 2838. And you have also explained what the process was about writing articles and sending articles and you said that an article to be published on a particular date would have to be sent, at the latest, the previous day at 8.00 in the evening. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also indicated that sometimes you would mention two places with a slash in between with Hamburg or another city where you had received information from. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you will recall that earlier I asked you what you had done on the 14th and following day. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your evidence today was that on the 14th, later in the day, or in the evening, I believe you said, you went to Tetovo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall what time that was, more or less?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case, let's me show you first ...

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is tab 51. It's Rule 65 ter 1D254.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what do you consider to be late evening, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, perhaps it is easier for you if you focus on the German version. Do you have the German version of the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is a piece called, in the translation in any case, "Macedonia -- is Learning to Watch Out for Albanian Tricks," and it's written by yourself and a person called Holge Wuchold. Do you agree? ?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see what is quite astonishing about that piece, apart from the fact that you would write about this issue and pay no attention to what you say -- what information you say about Ljuboten, but the piece is dated the 15th of August of 2001. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the locations that are mentioned are Berlin, Hamburg and Skopje. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose that Berlin and Hamburg would be the place where you would have obtained information from either Mr. Wuchold or someone else. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you can see from the content of that document, the part that relates to Macedonia rather than Germany or Brussels is in the first two paragraph. Do you agree with that? And the rest -- I mean, I'll ask to you look at the first two paragraph first. I'll read them for you. "There is peace on paper but in reality there is war. The Albanian rebels are involving the Macedonian forces in raging street battles in west Macedonian Tetovo. They even put a factory on fire. This factory was the most modern in the Balkan region and especially known for tailoring for Italian designers." Then another paragraph which says: "On top of that are the Macedonians from Tetovo and the surrounding villages on the run. UNHCR, the refugee aid is counting one to 5.000 refugees in Macedonia." Sir, would you agree that this first paragraph that I've read out to you and also to a lesser extent the second paragraph relate to events that were occurring in the Tetovo area at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree that this would mean - and again, there is no indication that you received that information from somewhere else, do you agree, in that article?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what I think is that was not a -- something I saw with my own eyes because otherwise I would have more described it and I don't remember if I saw street fighting in Tetovo on the -- on the 14th, no, I didn't see, because I haven't been in the city in this moment. I was together with the German soldiers, because what you say or what you see is we are going on to find out if the German soldiers will play a role in this Macedonian peace-building process.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's not what I see, Mr. Hutsch. What I see is an article published on the 15th which would therefore have to have been researched at the latest on the 14th. And it relates to events in the Tetovo area and you have indicated earlier that you don't write about places that you haven't been to or you would indicate that. So what that article suggests is that on the 14th you were in the Tetovo region. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's wrong. So we are -- we are in a semantic discussion about that what is called "ortsmarke" in German. That means what is written in the beginning of an article. So if in the moment in Iraq in complete Iraq, every day explodes ten car bombs, every journalist in Iraq would right in front "Baghdad" even if a car bomb explodes in Kirkuk or in Mosul, and it is not fair in this moment to say here we have -- we have Skopje here but you have been in Tetovo area and yet you are writing something. As far as I remember, the information about the street fightings in Tetovo came from two Macedonian sources and have been confirmed by an Albanian one by telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So I'll stop you there. Is your evidence now, Mr. Hutsch, that in fact you never went to Tetovo to obtain that information, that in fact you obtained that information about Tetovo from Skopje. Is that your current evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went to Tetovo, that means to the Erebino, if you want to have it precise, that means the German camp. Mr. Boskoski, I think, eight kilometres east of Tetovo, four kilometres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, the problem with this is you have indicated to the Chamber that you only reached Tetovo on the 14th in the evening at around 9.00 , which would be too late to contribute any information about Tetovo for this piece. So my question is this: Which one is a lie, that you went to Tetovo and obtained that information for the paper; or that, as you claimed earlier, you were in the village of Ljuboten on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the moment I don't see the widespread, I don't see. Sorry for that, because if I would have seen the street fightings in Tetovo, I think I would have described them much more. If you would compare that with other articles I did, exactly that you will find.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So what you are saying is, contrary to what you had claimed before about only writing about places where you had been, what you are telling now, if I understand you properly, is that you wrote about Tetovo without having any information or - let me rephrase that - without having made any personal observation of the events that you recount. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fair statement would have been that within some more sources, at least three, and with a phone call where in the background I heard shooting, somebody was telling me that in Tetovo Albanians and Macedonians security forces were fighting each other and that is what is written there. Then I was calling the -- the director of this factory, textile factory that was personally known to me because he was also manager of the Tetovo Theke hotel in which I used to stay longer before, and he has a weekend house in the [indiscernible] area. So she was telling me that this factory was shot up and -- and was set on fire, so now tell me where did a mistake? I don't see this mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the short answer to my question, Mr. Hutsch, is that you have written or contributed information to a piece which you signed about an event which did you not witness yourself, despite having assured the Chamber and the Prosecutor when he took interview that you would not write about events or incidents which you had not yourself witnessed. Is that correct? Unless you had -- unless you indicated that in your piece. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And if that is a critic to every journalism that is done by agencies, I'm willing to say I'm sorry, because that's normal daily life in journalism, but you are an expert for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you see, Mr. Hutsch, I think the problem is not one of journalism. I think the problem is is the truth of what you are saying. And I will ask the registry to bring Rule 65 ter 1D255, please. This is under tab 52 and it is ERN as 1D00-2691 in the German and 2693 in the English. Can you see this article in front of you, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is a piece which was dated the 16th of August of 2001 and it is called "Macedonia Count-down for the German Army Deployment." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it is written by Franz-Josef Hutsch, yourself, and the location is Hamburg. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is it correct that if the article was published on the 16th of August 2001 and that it mentions Hamburg as the place of writing, that would mean that you were in Hamburg already often the 15th of August. Is that correct? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that contradicts the evidence which you gave earlier to the Chamber that you had spent the rest of the week in Macedonia after what you said was a visit in Ljuboten on the 14th. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact if you prepared this article on the 15th in Hamburg, as this suggests, you would agree that that would suggest that you were travelling back to Germany on the 14th to be able to make it on time to prepare your article and send it to your editor? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree, and I will tell you why. Because I have here all the original articles I wrote in this time, and if we just have a look to the way I normally wrote articles, you will find that that is not my style. Second is, I wrote my last article on the 15th in Macedonia. It was published on 15th. That was the article we have seen. And the next article is 18/19, and there I have been in Hamburg and I have the original things here with me, and not the Internet things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we have received those directly from the Hamburger Adenblatt, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the original is quite more useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the original, Mr. Hutsch, mentioned the same dates and the dates can't lie. The article was published on the 16th, was written on the 15 in Hamburg, and you were travelling to Germany on the 14th. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what I'm put to go you, Mr. Hutsch, is that contrary to what you said - and I will come back to this matter - you were not in Skopje or in the Skopje area or around the Skopje area during the period 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 15 of August of 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm putting it to you to you, sir, that the statements that you've made about this period of time which I have just mentioned are, for the most part, false. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like now to turn to another date, Mr. Hutsch, if you permit. We'll go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, could I intervene? I'm sorry to interrupt, but I would like to be clearer in my mind. Mr. Hutsch, are you saying that you have an original in your possession of this article that is apparently published in the Hamburger newspaper for which you were reporting on the 16th of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what is the date when that original article, according to you, was written?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have this article in -- in the -- in the things that -- it was given by the Hamburger Adenblatt to me and you see these are the originals, and it is also not my handwriting. It is done by the secretary and she told me the last article was the 15th of August and the next one I wrote was the 18th and 19th of August. That means Saturday, Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I can also assist. I have just been told by our precious assistant that we received the original copies. If that is of any assistance to the Court, we will produce the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I'm still not quite clear what Mr. Hutsch is saying. You're saying that this article then was written in Hamburg or in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I suppose is just if I -- if I see what is going on that a fellow of mine, Thomas Frankenveld [phoen], did something together with the -- with agency material. Because the style, this article is written not my style to write. So I'm seeing this article now the first time. And have it as well not in the originals I have. And sometimes, sometimes they drop the name of an author over the article if you gave information to this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you agree that, according to the -- what was printed in the newspaper, you alone were the author.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it suggests that you were in Hamburg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree, but what I say is that an article like this one normally is not an article. That is overwritten with the full name, Your Honour, it is just signed with initials in the back, because that what I saw now is -- it's agency material. And just if you compare that to all other articles I was writing in this time, you will find that it is not my style to write.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you're saying this is not something that you yourself wrote?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Because I saw this -- this article -- I see that -- this article the first time, in this moment. And, for example, I never would write that two armoured infantry companies would have been part of the -- of the German -- of the German mission because it was all the time clear that it would have been parachuters, airborne infantry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry for having interrupted, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, are you suggesting that the paper like the Hamburger Adenblatt would publish article under your name without informing you or without giving you knowledge of the fact -- of this fact? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes things like that happen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that's a practice you say that is at least well-known in the Hamburger Adenblatt. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: My evidence is that it is happening in every newspaper that, for example, in the final edition there's missing one line, somebody is filing things like that with a name of an author, for example, or he is full filing this line with -- with material from agency, things like that. That happens in every newspaper. Even in Switzerland, in Germany and in Macedonia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, rather, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Hutsch, is that you were not in the places where you claim to have been during that period. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, we have a lot of -- a lot of eye-witnesses, and I presented these eye-witnesses -- I was talking to -- as well to you or to the Defence. And I think to clear this question, ask these eye-witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, I can assure you and the Court that I haven't talked to you at any time, or anyone in this team. But I would like to turn to the events of the 12th of August, if I may. And that would be the Sunday, when you say you went for the first time in Ljuboten. Do you recall saying that to this Court?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will briefly summarize your evidence on this, Mr. Hutsch, and if I make a mistake or if you feel there's anything to add, please do so. Your evidence is that, being certain that something would happen on that date, the 12th of August, you wake up earlier and you leave your hotel in Skopje accompanied by two interpreters, and you arrive in their company at the check-point in Radisani at around 7.15 to 7.20 that morning. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And upon your arrival there you say that you saw some police officer, and again correct me if I'm wrong, but I understand that you were saying that some of the police officers were the same as the one that you had seen the day before and with whom you had negotiated your so-called entrance fee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you explained both to this Chamber and to the Office of the Prosecutor that on that day, the 12th of August of 2001, you took notes during the day which you recorded chronologically into your notebook. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've also told the Office of the Prosecutor when you were interviewed by the OTP that on that day, the 12th of August of 2001, you eventually left the village of Ljuboten at what you say was 5.30 or 1730 on that day. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like first to ask you a number of questions about the check-point which you have mentioned in your statement and in evidence here. Do you agree that this police check-point which you've mentioned is the same one that you referred to in your evidence on the 10th, 11th and the 12th of August 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it's a check-point which you saw was located in a village called Radisani. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the entrance of Radisani, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Entrance or exit, depending which side you come from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is on the exit, if you wish, if you've come from Skopje when you go --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- towards Ljuboten, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you -- you have made a marking of that, do you recall, in one of the map that was shown to you by the Prosecution. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall in the immediate vicinity of that location which you've identified that there was a sort of a open space which serves, among other things, as a bus terminal. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A bus terminal?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: At the end of the village of Radisani there is a open space which you may or may not know serves as a bus terminal. If you don't know, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see a bus terminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Okay, Well, at this check-point, in any case, you indicated that on the 11th of August of 2001, you had negotiated what you represented as an entrance fee to be allowed to return the next day. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also suggesting that at that time you had been informed or you say you had been informed by police officer at that check-point that - and I'm quoting - "that is something, something for a operation was prepared, something there." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've also told this Chamber and the Prosecution when interviewed that from that check-point in Radisani on the 10th, you were -- 10th of August, you were able to see that a number of mortars had been fired into Ljuboten. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall saying also that --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, not -- I was able to see. I was able to hear. And that I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you recall saying in your statement and before this Tribunal that you had seen the two main areas of impacts of those mortars? Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in fact, the truth is that this did not happen. Is that correct? You didn't go to a check-point in Radisani?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You did not go to a check-point in Radisani on the 10th, you did not go to a police check-point in Radisani on the 11th and you did not go to a police check-point in Radisani on the 12th. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And also, what I'm putting to you is not only did you not see any mortar fired but you did not see any areas of impact, as you have claimed before this Tribunal. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is under tab 19. It's Rule 65 ter 1D313.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, a English version will appear. Thank you. Mr. Hutsch, this is a statement that was taken by the defence of Mr. Boskoski of a person called Saso Georgeivski, and Mr. Georgeivski is a police officer at the police station, the nearby police station of Cair. And I'll just draw your attention first to paragraph 3, which described who he is. It says this: "In 2001, I worked as a police officer. In August 2001, my post was at the police station Cair. The station was responsible inter alia for the village of Radisani and I worked as a police officer at that village in August 2001." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then we asked him specifically this, asked by the defence: "I can state that in August 2001, perhaps during the whole year of 2001, there was -- there never was a police or army check-point in the village of Radisani." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that rather contradicts your evidence. Would you agree, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So one of you would not be telling the truth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if I can draw your attention to the next paragraph it says this: "The road that passes through Radisani towards Ljuboten stayed open throughout the entire time, including the month of August 2001. As I already mentioned, there did not exist a check-point with vehicles or people would be stopped or prohibited from continuing towards the village of Ljuboten." Then I'm going go back to read the other paragraph of that statement, Mr. Hutsch. But do you agree that according to Mr. Georgievski, in any case, there was no check-point in Radisani at that time. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's another thing which, as you will see he contradicts you with, is your assertions that from that position in the village of Radisani, you were able to visualize the impact of mortars in Ljuboten. And you recall your evidence was at page -- on the 21st of June of 2007, at page 2502, 2503, among other things, and also in your statement. Before I proceed with that, do you recall the name of any of the police officers that you say were present on that day, the 10th, in Radisani at what you say was a check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you on your own or were you accompanied by anyone?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was accompanied.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell who accompanied you on that day?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both translators.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, I suppose you're still declining to mention the identity of these alleged persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think we have to draw upon the Wendell [phoen] decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree that had such persons existed, or if they existed, they would also have seen those things which you've described here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the problem, sir, is that there has been evidence in this trial, and also as you will see from Mr. Georgievski, that in fact not only did you not see what you claim to have seen, but you could not see it? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree, because I don't have the testimony of other people and I don't know if this person really exists, and I just know that since the accused have been in the Tribunal, the pressure on a lot of people in Macedonia rise higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, Mr. Hutsch, that our clients have anything to do that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just describing the fact. It's your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you explain how does that relate to what you were capable of observing from Radisani?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I say is that there were -- people were stopped, people were controlled. They had -- there were normal uniformed policemen. That's what I said, and that's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't talking about the policemen, sir. At this stage I'm asking you about the impacts of the mortar which you claim to have seen before this Chamber. Let me ask you this or let me --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you show me where I say that I saw the impacts from the check-point?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please bring up what is exhibit, I'm sorry, Rule 65 ter 1D234. Thank you. And I'll ask the registry, please, to bring up page 1D00-2571.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's page 5 of your statement, Mr. Hutsch. And I'll ask you to first focus on paragraph 25 and we will go down the numbers. This is what you said at paragraph 25 of your statement, and it relates, if you look at the previous page, to the 10th of August. It says this: "We stayed at this check-point for around an hour. It was my interest to get more information or at least to monitor more from this point since we were not allowed to proceed beyond this point." Then at paragraph 26 you say this: "I can mark this check-point on a map marked as attachment M1 at the position EM-0372 579." And then you go on to say this: "It was around 17 and 1800 hours when I noticed the impacts. I have heard mortars and I'm pretty sure that it came from 120-millimetre mortars. Six to nine mortar rounds were fired in the village of Ljuboten. I have seen mainly two areas of impacts." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I see and I'm looking for the point that I saw that from the check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, this is the paragraph that started two paragraph above, sir, because you say in paragraph 24: "The police check-point was obviously a regular police check-point." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 25 you say that you stayed at this check-point for around an hour and that you were not allowed to proceed beyond this point. Are you trying to put yourself in another position now, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you agree that you were at the check-point at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I agree is if you see a impact, I don't know if you ever saw a impact, you will see that something like a tower is rising up with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Pillar.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- smoke and dust and things like that between 25 and 30 metres. And that's what you couldn't see. And I'm telling, I have heard mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Hutsch, that's not what you said. What you said is this: "I have seen mainly two areas of impact."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's what you said. You're not talking about hearing, Mr. Hutsch, you're talking about seeing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw two areas of impact, with that what I saw, I'm sorry for that, I have just the word a tower like with dust, smoke and things like that. And that's what according to the rules of United Nations Military Observers is to identify target areas that you can't see yourself. And sorry for that, that we haven't been more precise in this statement, but what you can see is from this point these, I will say towers of dust.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, before we break, Mr. Hutsch, I will simply read to you what you had told the Prosecution at that time. It is the 21st of June of 2007. It's at page 2503 and it says this, question of Mr. Saxon. He was showing you this particular map, and we can see that you wrote the letters pointing to the inner circle above Radisani, you wrote the words CP. What does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That stands for check-point. Okay. "And a bit above and to the right, a bit to the north-east we see a couple of small circle and then another marking above it. Can you explain what those small markings are?" And you said: "These marking of first a mortar position here." Then Mr. Saxon asks: "A mortar position which -- what force? "By the -- probably by the Macedonian army," you said. "All right. And then below that, we see two little circles," and that's your answer, "These are two target areas where this mortar fired in while I was in the area of the check-point and I could monitor myself." So what you told the Prosecutor, Mr. Hutsch, in response to the question is that you could see more than smoke. You claim to have been able to see the mortars firing. That's what you said. That is page 2503?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That what you can see is first. If a mortar fires, you have a fire tower, that is rising between 10 and 15 metre over the mortar. And it is going on into a smoke and into a dust tower. And if you have impacts, you just see another tower with -- with dust and smoke. And both you could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps before I start again we'd simply indicate that if the Chamber wished to receive the original of the articles with the date, we have copies for the Judges here and with the assistance of the usher, and there should be a copy for the Prosecutor as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you recall that before the break I was asking you questions about what you claim were your observations, the observations that you made from Radisani. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact what I'm putting it to you, sir, is that none of the observation which you claim to have made on that day were yours; in other words, did you not see any of the things which you claim to have seen from that check-point. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to put to you, because you asked earlier about the evidence or the information provided by other people on that matter and on the 25th of May of 2007, a witness appeared before this Tribunal. It's a person who is referred to as Mr. M-83, and, Your Honour, this is at page 1494 to 1495 of the transcript. And he was asked this question that starts at line 21 of that page. He was asked "whether you noticed that there was gun-fire coming from one of the houses in Ljuboten and whether in your preparation for this evidence you were actually able to show this house to the Prosecution." "I saw this," he said, "at the moment, what it was about, were the people were, I can't say, because from Radisani you can't see Ljuboten because there is on a hill, Radisani is down in a hole." And that why, Mr. Hutsch, you could not have seen any of the things which you claim to have seen is because Radisani, in particular the place where you claim to have been, is straight in a hole and between Radisani and Ljuboten, there is a big nice hill. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree, because this check-point was in the area of a bridge, passing a small river, and even from there you could see -- you have a -- a view to the eastern part of Ljuboten. And you are going uphills in direction to Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So what this person called -- told the Trial Chamber was incorrect then. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: My evidence is that if you see the pictures that was made by the Prosecutor and which showed the -- the point where I have been, you can see exactly the roofs of -- of Ljuboten. And you can see much more than just the roofs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask you to have a look again at Rule 65 ter 1D313. This is, again, the statement, Mr. Hutsch, of Saso Georgievski and it is 1D00-2949 in the Macedonian and 2951 in the English. That is the same statement as I showed you earlier on. And this time I would ask you to look at paragraph 6, please, of that statement, and I will read it out to you. It says this: "In August 2001 there was a police patrol on the road that passes through Radisani and towards Ljuboten. At one point there was a permanent police patrol on the road where the bus station is located, but there was not a police check-point there, only police presence." Then he says: "It is physically impossible to see the village of Ljuboten from there. There is a hill between that position and the village of Ljuboten, which blocks the view between the two." So you would agree that the place which this witness refers to, which is right at the end of the village of Radisani on the way to Ljuboten, he says you can't see Ljuboten from there. Do you agree that's what he says?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, what I see is that this -- this person said there was not-- not a check-point, and in paragraph 6 he says, there has been a police presence, so what is the difference between a check-point and a police presence. Second, I don't know where the bus station is. I was locating the bus terminal where this bus terminal is, but what I say is that we have a bridge and if it is necessary for you, we will go there and I will show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps tomorrow if we have the time, Mr. Hutsch, we'll show you a few pictures, but do you agree that if one accepts the fact that the bus terminal is at the very end of the village in Radisani where you say you were and where you say there was a check-point and that the evidence of this person is that from that location you could not see Ljuboten, there would be a rather serious discrepancy with your evidence again. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree just on this point, that if we are talking from the same place, and the place I have been, what I think is much more north than this so-called bus terminal, I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, you've told me a bit earlier that you had no idea where this terminal was. Are you saying that now you recall where it is?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just looked to that paragraph 6, and immediately we have now a check-point or a police presence, whatever that means, and that is in a place what I think is much more south what he is describing a bus terminal, because I didn't see a bus terminal there where the check-point was. And what I say is if you are just going to this area and going into the field, probably after 100 and 200 metres you can see much more and we can go there and you will see exactly from that point that I was drawing to the map that you have a view to the eastern part of Ljuboten. And I'm not sure if the bus terminal that this police officer mentions that is playing now with the police presence, that this bus terminal is the same point where I identified this check-point. And that's -- that's what are you doing all the time, and now you're presenting yourself a document where somebody is confirming that there was a check-point after we have had a discussion for more than 30 minutes if there was a check-point or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you indicate, sir, where in the statement of Mr. Georgievski you see that he mentions the presence of a police check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is mentioning a police presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you interpret that to mean that there was a check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly that's what I'm interpreting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in fact if the police presence in question was a car with two policemen sitting in or outside of it, you would agree that this would not be a check-point or would you now suggest that it is in fact a check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say if that policeman would go and stop people and control them, in this moment it's a check-point. However how much they are, however how they equipped and however what they are doing and yourself presenting now to the Chamber a document where a police presence that you, you said that there was not a police presence, and this witness as well, said two paragraphs before that there was not a police presence, that immediately there was a police presence. Either if you define that now as a check-point or a police presence, it is up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well perhaps I'll ask you this, Mr. Hutsch: What did this alleged check-point look like in Radisani? What was it made of?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly that what I said, that there were police officers and police cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that's now corresponds exactly to the statement have you in front of you. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There have been some sand sacks [Realtime transcript read in error "some"] as well in the left side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry. The --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That doesn't correspond with what this man says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The transcript didn't pick it up. Did you mean sandbags?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sands sacks, sandbags.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was there anything else? Did you see a gun mounted or a beret or anything, anything else you saw there?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you're still claiming that there was reinforcement with sandbags on the side of the road. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some sandbags on the side of the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you is that you are changing your story all time, Mr. Hutsch. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree, because that is exactly what I said to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's -- are you suggesting that you mentioned to the Prosecutor that the check-point in question was made up just of a car, two policeman and a few sandbags?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there have been much more policemen in this moment, what I think up to six, eight, that some of them were dressed in a camouflage uniform And that there was a police car as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would like to ask the counsel and the witness to pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, that when you were interviewed for the first time by the Office of the Prosecutor in August of 2005 you described in chronological fashion what you said had happened in Ljuboten on the 12th of August; that's the Sunday. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask that the witness be shown again his statement. That is Rule 65 ter 1D234. And I will ask the registry to turn to page 1D00-2576. Do you recall, Mr. Hutsch, also telling the Office of the Prosecutor that a duty book was kept at the check-point which you said you saw in Radisani. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- I was talking about -- about notices one officer made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you recall suggesting to the Prosecution that a duty book was kept by the police at the check-point? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the statement please not be shown at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the duty -- we were -- we were looking for a description what was going on. And what I think is now if it is very important for you, and that's exactly the point I made with my mother tongue, I'm not sure if they have duty books or log-books or whatever else you will call them in check-points but one of these officer had notices and he was making notices.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So can we agree that you told the Prosecution that there was some sort of a document on paper in which information was noted down by the police officer? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But I don't know if he was doing these notices because he was doing that for himself or if that was officially ordered, I don't know. I'm not familiar with that, and just with my experience in the El Masri case, I know that there have been some -- some books in the border stations where they -- where the Macedonian authorities write in that -- that somebody enter Macedonia or leave Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness now please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D234, please. It will be page 1D00-2576. Thank you. And if you could enlarge the top of the page, please. Do you recall, Mr. Hutsch, that you described in chronological fashion what you said you knew about the events of Ljuboten of the 12th of August of 2001, and the first such incident which you recorded or you recalled was one that took place at 603 and you will make it clear later that you didn't have that of personal knowledge. But I would like to read to you these few paragraphs. At paragraph 59 it says this: "0603 hours. The 120-millimetres rounds were fired by the army into the direction of the village." Then at paragraph 60 of your statement you say: "0711 hours a second round of mortar rounds were fired from the army position into the village." And then at paragraph 61 you make it clear -- you make the following clear: "The above information of 0603 hours and 0711 hours is hearsay information and was told to me by some police officers from the check-point in Radisani. The police officers took this information from the duty book at the check-point and they also elaborate to me the location where these grenades impacted. I will mark these impacts on the panoramic picture, PP3." So you agree that as far as your statement is concerned and as far as it was taken by the Office of the Prosecutor, they understood you to say that this information about those two particular incidents had been taken or given by you from a -- from the policemen, their duty book at the check-point. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that's what is written, but I remember exactly that we have had the discussion if that -- that have been notices or whatever. And I don't know if these police officer was taking his notices or if that was a official duty book or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, first I'll ask you this. You've indicated that at the check-point on that day on the 12th you saw a number of policemen, and I think you mention the number. Did you see anyone else at what you call the check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you see, this evidence is directly contradicted once again by the evidence of another witness who has already given evidence in this case and who had come precisely from the village of Radisani on that very day and who went towards the village of Ljuboten. But contrary to you, this person did not mention any check-point in Radisani but what he mentioned is that there was a immense crowd of civilians is there. So you would agree that what he saw and --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be Mr. Bolton. It's on the 7 of June, 2007, page 1686 to 1687.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Greatly differs from your description of those events. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in which times Bolton had been there, where he had been, so I don't know where Mr. Bolton and -- exactly has been and at what time he has been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you see, Mr. Bolton spent almost the entire day in the area around the village of Ljuboten and Radisani.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see nothing what Mr. Bolton said. I see just that what are you telling me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the other thing that I'm putting to you, sir, is that if Mr. Bolton is to be believed that, as he said, that was a great crowd of civilians on the road between Radisani there and Ljuboten, you did not mention seeing a single such person in your statement. Do you agree with that and again today?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that there was not a crowd of people in the outskirts, if you want to say that, or on the entrance of Radisani.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if Mr. Bolton were to give that evidence that in fact between Radisani where had you come from and Ljubanci on that road, there was a great crowd of people showing a great amount of animosity towards him and the other people, you would say that this is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that, because I don't know when Mr. Bolton was passing the street. I don't know where he saw this crowd and where he became -- this reactions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the fact is, and you will agree with that, that you did not mention seeing any of that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see a bigger crowd in Radisani at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct, as you confirmed earlier to me, that you explained to the Chamber that on the 11th of August or, rather, on the 12th of August at 7.00 a.m., around 7.00 a.m. when you said you reached the check-point in Radisani, you saw some of the same policemen that you had seen the previous day at around 1530 on the 11th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you see --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, on the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the 12th is the Sunday.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The 11th is the --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- the Saturday. So that would be the 12th and the 11th?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You see, one problem we have here is that even if such a check-point had existed at that time, Mr. Hutsch, the same people could not have been at the check-point at the time and I'm going to show you why.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn once again to what is Rule 65 ter 1D313, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before we move on to the next topic, I have reviewed pages 1686 to pages 1687 of the transcript, and I'm wondering if Mr. Mettraux can tell us where there is a reference to a crowd of civilians. There are references to civilians but where is there a reference to crowd of civilians, from the testimony of Mr. Bolton?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we can -- I can read the passage, Your Honour, if you wish. It starts like this: "You could confirm that you did not enter the village on that day, is that correct?" "That's correct." "And do I understand properly that the reason why you did not or could not enter the village on that day was because of the animosity of the civilians or some civilians in any case that were around the village and the animosity which they showed to your team is that correct?" "There was when we approached when we tried to approach the village initially right at the beginning, following the mine strike there was animosity from the villager in Ljubanci. Subsequently we did not meet with animosity when trying to approach Ljuboten from the other direction which was further to the east, avoiding Ljubanci." "And was there any particular reason why you did not attempt to enter the village on that day? Was it the same animosity?" "There was no animosity but there was a determination on one occasion not to let us pass and there was also occasion where we were stopped by the police." "And did you ask it -- did you ask to it go through or was it your own determination that the risk was too great to get into the village on that day?" "We had no intention to drive into the middle of an exchange of fire, but nonetheless, we were on the occasion stopped by civilians." Sir, to go back to the issue that were mentioned to you earlier, I would like to ask you to now turn to paragraph 8 of the document in front of you. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe explain something to me. Mr. Bolton says that he was stopped by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I was referring to is not who stopped him, Mr. Hutsch, but the presence of --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking if I'm saying the truth that I was stopped by the police the whole time. We are discussing this topic now since 60 minutes, and here Mr. Bolton says that he was stopped by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No. What I asked you, Mr. Hutsch, is whether you had seen any civilians or any angry civilians on that location and you said no, that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think your emphasis was rather on a crowd of civilians, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that was the evidence that Mr. Bolton gave in his statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, which is also admitted and which was reiterated in the terms that I read out in the -- and in the investigator's notes which were used also with Mr. Bolton when he explained the reason why they could not enter on that occasion. We believe that the statement or the passage that was read right now reflects the fact that there was indeed a crowd or at least a number of civilians along the road from Radisani to Ljubanci and Ljuboten, which Mr. Bolton gave evidence about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the interpretation you place on the evidence. It is not expressly so stated by the evidence, and it is a matter about which different conclusions could be formed, I think, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, if I can ask to you turn to paragraph 8 of the statement which is in front of you. It is the statement again of Mr. Saso Georgievski and it says this: "I have also been asked about the shifts of the police. I can state the following. The shifts were determined upon an order by the commander. They are shifts according to five systems. From system one -- from system number one to system number five. System number one means working all the time non-stop; system number two means 12 hours working and 12 hours rest. I think that in August 2001, system two was the one according to which the work was conducted." I will ask you the question and I'll come back in a minute to another matter, Mr. Hutsch, but would you agree that if the statement of Mr. Georgievski is correct again, and according to the police shift system at the time, you could not have seen the same people on the 11th of August at 1530 and at 7.00 a.m. on the 12th. Do you agree that this would not be possible?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not -- that's not impossible, because especially when there was going on an operation in an area, the people stood on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that according to Mr. Georgievski, the system would have prevented -- or would -- would have precluded the possibility that the same person be there at the same time. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. He is talking about the shift. That means how the police forces were structured and organised and were playing under normal circumstances how they was doing their job, and we have had in the time from the 10th up to the -- I will say 12th or 13th -- you are listening to me or do you need a minute for your documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Don't worry about me, Mr. Hutsch, just go on with your evidence.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
